_comment: Human-maintained gate for FAR defined-term links (plan §12.2/§12.3, §37; rules in far_aim/links/definitions.py). Terms are verbatim term text as the definitions section prints it (trailing punctuation included). deny: never link this definition — from every source that defines the text, or, with "section", only from that definitions section (e.g. {"term": "Airport", "section": "139.5"}). Every entry needs a reason; an entry naming a term no source of the accepted eCFR issue defines fails the build.

deny.reason: Appears on nearly every page ('FAA Form', 'FAA-approved'); the § 1.2 expansion is not what those uses turn on.

§ 1.1 defines a cockpit device; the text mostly says 'instrument rating', 'instrument approach', 'instrument runway', which are not that device. Multiword § 1.1 terms such as 'Instrument approach procedure (IAP)' still link.
Beyond the § 1.1 airman/aircraft senses the text says 'type certificate', 'type design', 'type of operation'; the word alone cannot tell them apart.
Beyond the § 1.1 airman/aircraft senses the text says 'Class B airspace' and 'class of airspace'.
Beyond the § 1.1 airman/aircraft senses the text says 'transport category', 'approach category' and 'Category II'.
§ 1.1's Category A is a rotorcraft certification category; Parts 97 and 135 use 'Category A' for an approach category.
§ 1.1's Category B is a rotorcraft certification category; Part 97 uses 'Category B' for an approach category.
